articleTitle: An Investigation of the Rotor Position Influence on the Broadband Phase Impedance - Application to SFRA Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: Sweep Frequency Response Analysis (SFRA) applied to rotating machines diagnosis and monitoring lacks of widespread industrial applicability up to this date. Several authors identify the rotor position influence as one of the main obstacles for an on-site and cost-effective diagnosis. This work provides a thorough investigation on how the rotor affects the broadband phase impedance of a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine (PMSM). The study is developed in several stages including analytical, Finite Element Analysis (FEA) and experimental measurements. The rotor field is identified as the main cause for the rotor position influence. In addition, the magnetic excitation of the stator coils and thus, the coil distribution, play a significant role on the broadband impedance variation.

articleTitle: Fault-Tolerant and Voltage Balancing Control for Five-Phase Three-Level T-type Inverters under Open-Switch Faults
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: The reliability of the system is a demanding challenge in many application fields, such as automotive, aerospace, renewable energies, and other industrial applications. Multiphase machines and drives suit this request due to their inherent fault-tolerant capability. However, to allow post-fault operation, a dedicated control technique must be developed. Multilevel converters improve the performance of the machine in terms of currents and torque ripples. Moreover, the multilevel converters provide many degrees of freedom to the system and are more flexible during an Open Phase Fault (OPF) or Opens Switch Fault (OSF). In this paper, a fault-tolerant technique for five-phase three-level T-type inverters under Open Switch Fault is developed. The OSF is analyzed while considering the voltage balancing of the dc-bus capacitors. Some simulation results are provided to verify the feasibility of the proposed solution.

articleTitle: Spectral Entropy and Frequency Cepstral Coefficients of Stray Flux Signals for Sparking Detection in DC Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: In this work, the use of stray flux signals is proposed to detect sparking faults in the commutation system of DC motors. The proposed method uses an algorithm based on the spectral entropy of stray-flux signals. This is combined with a quantitative indicator of the sparking activity that is based on the Mel frequency cespstral coefficients. The proposed algorithm is applied to flux signals captured both under the starting and at steady state to comparatively evaluate the results and analyze their feasibility to be used as the basis of the sparking detection method. The results prove the potential of the proposed approach for sparking fault detection and assessment in DC motors as well as its suitability for possible future incorporation in stand-alone diagnosis systems.

articleTitle: Modelling and Analysis of PM Demagnetization and its Effect on Vibration in SPM Machines
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: This paper presents a modelling technique to estimate the changes in vibration spectrum due to non-uniform demagnetization. A modulation function is defined that accounts for the nature of demagnetization in the magnets. Using this function and the conformal mapping based approach, the field distribution in the air-gap is obtained. As this approach is semi-analytical, the electromagnetic step of performing vibration spectrum analysis of a machine become faster. The modulation function introduces the effects of magnet demagnetization into the air-gap flux density. The mechanical stress distribution obtained from the field distributions is fed to mechanical harmonic response solver to estimate the level of acceleration corresponding to the particular frequencies of vibration. The results and discussion related to the extent of demagnetization and the corresponding changes in vibration spectrum are presented.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation of High Viscosity on Oil Spray Cooling System with Hairpin Winding
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: The growing electric propulsion systems market directly affects electric motors’ current density. This leads to higher power density electric motors that limit utilizing only conventional thermal management systems. As a result, it is essential to integrate this conventional thermal management system with an advanced cooling system. Oil spray cooling is an advanced thermal management system that provides enormous heat transfer; however, it faces some drawbacks occur by oil as the high viscosity coolant. This paper uses an experimental approach to consider the challenges of the high viscosity of coolant on temperature uniformity and nozzle performance.

articleTitle: Preliminary Analysis of Mechanical Bearing Faults for Predictive Maintenance of Electrical Machines
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: Nowadays, electrical machines are used in numerous applications, where unexpected faults are to be prevented. Sophisticated technologies are demanded to be able to manage big data of machines conditions and store these datasets remotely using cloud computation. This data is necessary for algorithms to be trained and predict further failures. This paper presents a study of bearing faults for predictive maintenance. The data collection in lab environment and its preliminary analysis is introduced. The impact of different control modes and loads on global parameters of rotating machines is discussed. The fault classification and prediction techniques are presented.

articleTitle: Outer Bearing Race Diagnosis by Means of Stray Flux Signals and Shannon Entropy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: Bearings are a fundamental element that allows rotary movement in electric motors. It becomes essential for its operation under optimal conditions. However, it is one of the elements that tend to be most affected due to various inherent causes of its operating conditions. Although multiple methodologies have been proposed for diagnosing bearing faults, these are usually invasive, and the gradualness of the failure is not generally studied, nor is the behavior in various materials (ceramic, metallic, hybrid, etc.). This work proposes a non-invasive methodology based on analyzing magnetic stray flux signals using the Shannon entropy as an indicator to detect outer race failures under different degrees of wear damage and different construction materials. The obtained results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, which is validated on a kinematic chain (composed of a 0.746 KW induction motor, a belt and pulleys transmission system, and an alternator as a load).

articleTitle: Detection of Lithium Plating in Li-ion Batteries for Electric Vehicle Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: This paper investigates the lithium plating problem in Li-ion batteries and proposes a diagnostic method of the lithium plating which is properly adapted to be used in electric automotive applications. The suggested lithium plating diagnostic method is based on the analysis of the cell impedance that is estimated by utilizing the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) method. The EIS technique is realized by using a sinusoidal excitation current that is superimposed on the battery cell current, while the impedance is determined by adopting the single frequency method where the excitation signals is composed by sinusoidal currents of individual sequential frequencies. When the lithium plating is developed in a battery cell, its impedance is decreased and therefore, by monitoring it, the lithium plating can be identified in real-time. The functionality and practicality of the proposed lithium plating detection technique for using it in real-time in electric vehicle applications is experimentally verified and selective experimental results for several battery charging and temperature operating conditions are presented.

articleTitle: Real Time Core Loss Estimation for the Wound Rotor Synchronous Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: Estimation of electrical losses for machines is important to operating them efficiently. Although copper loss is typically the dominant form of electrical losses in an electric machine, core loss also contributes significantly especially at high speed. In this study, two simple analytical model for core loss are proposed for the wound rotor synchronous machine using the least squares method and validated through FEA simulation. The proposed core loss estimation methods have 12% and 53% average error over all operating points of the machine. They are extremely light computationally and use very few coefficients making them viable options for real-time controllers for various applications.

articleTitle: Particular Winding Configuration in Permanent Magnet Traction Motors enabling Voltage Weakening under Overspeed and Fault Tolerance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: The paper introduces a particular winding configuration in permanent magnet motors involving appropriate additional magnetic circuits in stator end winding region; such a technique enables substantial improvement of voltage weakening in high speed ranges as well as appropriate reduction of fault currents. The additional magnetic circuit presence can be incorporated in the motor design procedure by adopting a 2D coupled finite element field analysis and equivalent circuit approach. A methodology based on a particular reduced scalar potential technique decreases importantly the necessitated computational means by tackling the 3D field configuration in end winding zone parts to an appropriate 2D axisymmetric one. The proposed methodology is implemented in a particular 25 kW multi layer permanent magnet traction motor.

articleTitle: Detection of Harmonics by using Parallel-Connected Nonlinear Limit Cycle Oscillators
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: Harmonic distortion in three-phase power systems has become a relevant problem and many research efforts are focused on the detection of harmonic components. Several existing tools have been reported in the literature to extract data from current and voltage signals and most of these tools are based on linear filters. However, non-linear tools have been barely used to detect harmonics. In this paper, a method to detect positive and negative sequence components of harmonics based on parallel-connected limit cycle oscillators is presented. The proposed method can be seamlessly applied for power system monitoring in order to extract harmonics of the fundamental frequency, even in the case of frequency fluctuations. In addition, it can be applied for harmonic diagnostic in three-phase electric machines. The performance of the proposed technique is validated through simulations performed in Matlab/Simulink. Results show that the proposed technique can be used to extract all the required details from harmonics in three-phase systems.

articleTitle: The effect of heat sink thermal capacitance and resistance on predicted lifetime of switching devices in photovoltaic applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: When using state-of-the-art-lifetime estimation techniques for switching devices, the thermal load of the component is an important input for the lifetime models. As a result, thermal capacitance and convective resistance of the heat sink play an important role in lifetime predictions. This study investigates the sensitivity of switching device lifetime predictions to thermal capacitance and resistance of the heat sink considering two 1 year mission profiles: Arizona and Oldenburg. Results show that thermal capacitance can suppress the lifetime consumption of shorter cycles. This is especially the case in Oldenburg because of its variable weather profile. Ignoring thermal capacitance can result into a mean time to failure underestimation of 70.4% in Oldenburg and 36.5% in Arizona. It is also found that the mission profile time resolution is important for lifetime predictions.

articleTitle: A Domain Adaptation Method Based on Deep Coral for Rolling Bearing Fault Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: As a key component of motor, the operating status of rolling bearings directly affects the overall function and performance of each mechanism system of mechanical equipment The traditional rolling bearing intelligent fault diagnosis method has problems such as requiring a large amount of in-service data for fault analysis, poor generalization capability, etc. In addition, it is extremely costly to obtain labeled rolling bearing high quality condition data. Transfer learning is one of the methods that can effectively solve the above problems. In this paper, we propose a transfer learning model based on Coral transfer loss function as a rolling bearing fault diagnosis method. The model uses ResNet50 as the feature extractor, Coral loss function as the transfer loss function, and CrossEntropyLoss as the classification loss function. Finally, we validated the feasibility of the proposed method by using the Case Western Reserve University bearing dataset under variable operating conditions, the model was validated with correct transfer rates of over 90% for all twelve transfer types; which greatly surpasses other typical transfer learning fault diagnosis methods, which proved the rationality of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Determination of Dominant Influencing Factors on Partial Discharge Inception Voltage
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: With the increasing interest in adopting higher DC link voltage and fast switching devices in electric drives for electrified transportation, the partial discharge (PD) risk of electrical machines boosts compromising the drive integrity. The PD inception mechanism is simultaneously affected by both ambient conditions and voltage characteristics. By determining the dominant influencing factor on partial discharge inception voltage (PDIV), the preliminary reliability assessment would be made easier since the impact of secondary factors could be temporarily neglected. In this paper, the influence of three environmental conditions (i.e., pressure, temperature, and relative humidity) and three voltage characteristics parameters (i.e., rise time, switching frequency, and duty cycle) on PDIV is studied. The results suggest that PDIV is most influenced by environmental conditions while the characteristics of test voltage have less impact on PDIV.

articleTitle: Stray Flux Signal Analysis for Faults Detection in Induction Motors During Startup Transient By Means Of Statistical Indicators
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: Electric motors are one of the most used primary drivers for diverse processes involving rotary movement in several fields concerning modern societies. One of the most widespread types of electric motors is Induction Machines (IMs), mainly due to their robustness, easy control, and easy maintenance. Despite their excellent characteristics and robustness, IMs are prone to fail from different constructive parts. One of the most common failures is due to broken rotor bars (BRBs). Although multiple methodologies have been proposed for diagnosing BRBs, these are mainly based on methods that rely on the amplitudes of specific fault-related frequencies, which may yield false diagnoses. More recently, transient methods based on tracking fault-related time-frequency (t-f) patterns involve using t-f methods with a high computational load, and sometimes the resolution may need to be better. This paper proposes a novel non-invasive low-burden method for the diagnosis of BRBs and misaligments. The proposal relies on the computation and amplitude tracking of stray-flux-based statistical indicators from signals captured during the startup transient. The results demonstrate the proposed method's effectiveness, validated on a kinematic chain (composed of a 0.746 KW induction motor, a belt and pulleys transmission system, and an alternator as a load).

articleTitle: FEM Analysis of Demagnetization Risk of Flux-Switching Machine Under Short Circuit Condition Considering Machine Temperature
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: In this paper, the demagnetization risk of a flux-switching machine for low-voltage automotive drives is analyzed considering the machine temperature. Both nominal operation with maximum current and fault cases are investigated. Single-phase and three-phase short circuits are considered as fault cases. It can be seen that even in nominal operation the magnets can be partially demagnetized. The machine geometry is therefore optimized in such a way that magnet demagnitization is avoided both in nominal operation and in the event of a fault.

articleTitle: Two-winding procedure for the measurement of the anhysteretic curve points of ferromagnetic materials
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: At a first approximation and sufficiently low frequencies, two macroscopic phenomena influence the hysteresis cycle shape in ferromagnetic materials: magnetic hysteresis and magnetic saturation. Different magnetic models use the anhysteretic curve as a fundamental locus in the magnetic material representation. In the literature, many authors proposed easier measurement methods to obtain the anhysteretic curve, or methods, which envisage the use of standard equipment already available on the market. In the present work, a measurement procedure is outlined, involving only two windings, being partly or fully compliant with the sample preparation described in the 60404 standards. Additionally, the proposed method is suitable to measure the small-signal permeability in each point of the anhysteretic curve right after the determination of the point itself. The method is executed on three toroidal samples made of different materials: a laminated sheet, a Soft Magnetic Composite and an amorphous ferrite core. The results are then compared with those of a very low frequency, large cycle conventional measurement, showing a good matching with the expected anhysteretic behaviour of the three materials.

articleTitle: Exciter Field Winding Temperature-Based Condition Monitoring Method for Brushless Synchronous Machines
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: Although the provision of excitation power is a critical aspect to the operation of brushless synchronous machines, there is no technical development in specific condition monitoring methods for exciter field windings. Exciter field windings can be affected by various faults, such as interturn faults due to insulation failures or electrical continuity losses due to connection failures. In order to provide a specific condition monitoring method for these windings, in this paper a novel method is presented based on the comparison of the measured winding resistance and winding temperature at each operating point with respect to a healthy temperature-resistance characteristic. The applicability of the method has been confirmed through experimental tests on the exciter of a 4900-kVA alternator, obtaining promising results.

articleTitle: Optimal Feature Selection via Bayesian Optimisation for Acoustic Condition Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: Efficient diagnosis of machine faults is important for predictive maintenance and asset management of industrial systems. This paper investigates acoustic techniques as a non-destructive and resource-optimized alternative for machine fault diagnosis. Relevant data analysis techniques usually involve signal time-frequency analysis, feature extraction, and fault classification. However, there are many feature sets that can be extracted, some of which may be redundant or even cause negative effect to the fault classification task. Thus, it is beneficial to select the most informative features for solving a specific task. This paper investigates the use of Bayesian optimization to select the optimal acoustic features, and the method is validated using a laboratory case study for bearing fault diagnosis. This feasibility study helps set up a machine learning framework for further meta-model development that could select optimal features, models and hyperparameters simultaneously.

articleTitle: A Ground Fault Detection Method for Double Fed Induction Machines
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: The use of Double Fed Induction Machines (DFIM) is widely implemented in wind farms and pumping stations due to their regulation capacity. The rotor of DFIMs is one of the most expensive parts of these installation. They are usually connected to low power converters to vary the machine operation point changing the frequency of the rotor. However, the injection of pulsed voltages in the rotor causes high insulation stresses and the deterioration of these machines. If the insulation fails, a ground fault can be originated which can damage the machine. In this field, this paper proposes a new method to detect ground faults in power converter fed DFIMs. The method consists of a grounding resistor in the midpoint of the DC bus where the voltage is measured. With the frequency response of this measurement, ground faults can be detected not only in the DFIM’s rotor but also in its stator or even in its own converter DC bus. To corroborate the method, numerous simulations carried out in Matlab Simulink are presented, achieving positive results.

articleTitle: Alpha-Beta Plane Current Modulus Slot Harmonics in Symmetrical Six-Phase Induction Motors Fed by Unbalanced Voltages and Under Stator Faults
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: Inter-turn short-circuit faults diagnostics in induction motors under unbalanced supply voltage conditions has been a challenging task since both conditions affect the machine in the same manner. An investigation of two harmonic components (related to the principal slot harmonics) of the alpha-beta plane current modulus signature is addressed to detect stator faults in a symmetrical six-phase induction motor fed by unbalanced voltages. Experimental results, including different load torques, fault severities, and unbalanced supply voltage levels show that the detection of stator faults without being affected by the presence of unbalanced supply voltage conditions can be achieved efficiently without adding complexity to the diagnostics methodology.

articleTitle: The Use of The Line Impedance Symmetrical Components for Stator Faults Detection and Location in Symmetrical Six-Phase Induction Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: This paper addresses the detection of inter-turn short-circuit faults in symmetrical six-phase induction motors (S6PIM). The fault diagnostic is conducted by applying a non-intrusiveness signal-based fault diagnostic technique based on the symmetrical components analysis of the line impedance. This technique allows the fault severity evaluation and the identification of the faulty motor phase, facilitating the implementation of fault-tolerant control strategies. The presented experimental results, for different load torques and fault scenarios, demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed technique.

articleTitle: Detection of Corrosion in Ball Bearings in Synchronous Reluctance Motors through the Computation of Statistical Indicators of Current Signals
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: Bearing faults are the among the most common faults in electric motors. Their detection is usually carried out through the analysis of vibration data. However, there are some cases in which this technique cannot be applied. One of the alternatives is the analysis of current signals to diagnose the bearing condition. On the other hand, there is a growing interest in synchronous reluctance motors (SynRM) due to their low cost and higher reliability. Nevertheless, there is little literature on bearing faults in synchronous reluctance motors. This work proposes the computation of statistical indicators obtained from the time-frequency maps of the current signal envelope to detect the presence of corrosion in bearings of SynRM. It is proven that these indicators not only detect the presence of the fault but are promising tools to determine its severity.

articleTitle: Analysis and Minimization Scheme for Torque Ripple of Single-Pole Demagnetized PMSM
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: This paper investigates the impact of single-pole demagnetization on the flux-linkage and torque ripple of a permanent-magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) with a concept of effective area. Through linear regression analysis, it is confirmed that the effective area of a single-pole does not significantly change with levels of demagnetization. Based on the analysis, a current reference generator is proposed to minimize torque ripple from a single-pole demagnetization using instant MTPA commands. The proposed method is validated through finite element analysis (FEA)-based simulations. The findings contribute to the understanding of the effects of single-pole demagnetization on PMSMs and provide a practical approach for reducing torque ripple in single-pole demagnetized PMSMs.

articleTitle: A Ground Fault Location Method for Modular Multilevel Converters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: The need of efficient electric transmission systems, the rise of renewable energy production and battery storage systems has empowered the use of Modular Multilevel Converters (MMC) which allows a better performance than convenctional converters. However, the diagnosis of electrical faults in MMC are more challenging because more components are involved in the fault circuit. Particularly, ground faults are the most common type of faults in power systems and their diagnosis has not been widely studied for AC-DC converters, where most of the industrial relays fail. This paper proposes a ground fault location method for MMC converters based on a high value grounding resistor placed in a DC midpoint or AC neutral point of the MMC. Measuring the voltage between its terminals and performing its frequency analysis the fault can be located. The novelty of this method resides in the detection of the ground fault in AC or DC side or in the faulty-submodule location if the ground fault happens inside the MMC. To corroborate the method, numerous simulations have been performed in a half-bridge three-phase MMC converter obtaining promising results.

articleTitle: Parameter Identification For Inter Turn Fault Detection In Permanent-Magnet Synchronous Motors Using Stator Flux Linkage DC Offset Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: The parameters of PMSM with inter-turn fault are identified using a time-stepping finite element method (FEM). Analytical expressions (AE) uses the estimated parameters for fault analysis similar to FEM analysis. The fault waveforms, terminal voltages, obtained from the AE models are used for inter turn fault (ITF) detection, using Stator Flux Linkage DC offset (SFDO). A comparison is made between the SFDOs obtained using AE with two sets of parameters and experimental results under different fault severity. The difference in parameter selection depends on the fault severity in induced voltage waveform and in all three phases, which makes AE-based fault modeling and its detection more accurate compared to the case where only the no load waveform is used for all three phases.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Permanent-Magnet Synchronous Motor Drives: Two-level GaN-Based and Three-level Silicon-Based Voltage Source Inverters
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: Gallium Nitride (GaN) transistors, which fall into the category of Wide-bandgap semiconductors, have higher switching capability and typically smaller conduction losses in low voltage when compared to traditional Silicon (Si)-based MOSFET counterparts. Due to these promising features, they are progressively becoming popular in power electronics applications including motor drives. Permanent-Magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) are gaining significant interest in many drive applications due to their several advantages including high efficiency, high power density, and reduced weight and size. This paper discusses the application of two-level (2L) voltage-source inverter (2L-VSI) with GaN switches and three-level VSI (3L-VSI) with high-end MOSFET switches in PMSM drive systems and compares them in terms of switching performance, power loss, efficiency, and the voltages generated at the PMSM terminals through considering the detailed models of the semiconductor switches. Moreover, the overvoltage and high dv/dt effects due to the connecting cables between VSI and PMSM are studied and a solution to reduce these negative effects is investigated. Simulations carried out using PSIM software are presented.

articleTitle: Auto-Adaptive Stator Ground Fault Protection for Synchronous Generators in Diesel-Electric Locomotives
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: Diesel-electric locomotives are equipped with one or more synchronous generators driven by diesel engines, that provide the necessary electrical energy for their operation. These generators are usually provided with some protection relays, depending on their rated power and their type of service. Standard stator-ground fault protection has a setting for rated conditions. In case of variable speed and voltage operation, the protection does not cover all the operation range of the machine. In addition, unwanted tripping may occur due to incorrect filtering of the third harmonic. In this paper, an auto-adaptative stator ground protection function is presented, for the operation of synchronous machines at variable voltage and frequency. A specific case study is tackled, focused on the main generators of a diesel-electric locomotive. Numerous simulations are carried out to verify the proposed protection method. The obtained results are promising, and they can be used in other synchronous machines operating at variable speed.

articleTitle: Detection of Multiple Open Faults in Variable Phase-Pole Machines based on Harmonic Plane Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: Multiphase electrical machine are inherently true fault tolerant, which is a key difference as compared to conventional three-phase machines. The subgroup of variable phase-pole machines have the ability to change phase-pole configurations only through current control. Due to the higher availability and simpler construction, three-phase voltage source inverters modules are often used for multiphase electrical machines. While many approaches exist for one single open-phase fault, this paper proposes an open-fault detection method capable to detect the failure of an entire three-phase module for variable phase-pole machines. It is an extension to the harmonic-plane-decomposition fault detection analyzing the instantaneous space harmonic content of the current distribution. Simulation results demonstrate the feasibility of the approach.

articleTitle: Influence of DC Link Capacitor Ageing on Performance of Single-Phase Power Factor Correction Rectifiers
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: Coefficients of PI controller, typically employed as DC link voltage loop compensator of power factor correction rectifiers (PFCR) depend on DC link voltage reference, grid voltage magnitude, grid frequency and DC link capacitance so that desired values of grid-side current total harmonic distortion (THD) and DC-link voltage loop phase margin (PM) are attained. On the other hand, it is well-recognized that DC link capacitor ageing leads to reduction of corresponding capacitance value. Consequently, this paper investigates the influence of the latter on the above-mentioned performance merits as well as on the crossover frequency of DC link voltage loop and steady-state DC link voltage ripple. Frequency-domain and time-domain simulations are provided to successfully verify the derived analytical expressions.

articleTitle: Identification of sensitive feature in the stray magnetic field to detect rotor short-circuit fault in synchronous generators
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: This paper presents an application of the external magnetic field measured in the vicinity of a synchronous generator in a hydroelectric powerplant for the detection of a rotor short circuit fault. The measurement of the external magnetic field was performed using a flux sensor and the analysis of the signal is done in a quantitative and qualitative way by considering the spectral evolution of the signal but also its temporal variation. The presented results are obtained analyzing several operating conditions of a 55 MW generator in healthy and fault case. We notice the interest of using the reduced values in percentage to better compare the different state of the machines. A vibration study is also presented at the end of the paper to complete the analysis.

articleTitle: Detection of External Rotor PMSM Inter-Turn Short Circuit Fault using Extended Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: The presence of an inter-turn short circuit in electrical machines can lead to the complete shutdown of the system and cause disturbances in operation. In this paper, a diagnosis method for the detection of a stator inter-turn short circuit fault on an external rotor permanent magnet synchronous motor is proposed. The detection approach is based on the Extended Kalman Filter, which continuously estimates the different quantities of the machine. The designed technique is based on a comparison of the estimated and measured stator currents. An analysis of the signals resulting from the comparison is used to detect and locate the fault. Simulation results are presented to validate the proposed fault detection and diagnosis approach.

Author Keywords: external rotor permanent magnet synchronous motor

articleTitle: Influence of Rotational Speed on the Frequency Response Analysis of the Field Winding of Large Hydrogenerators
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: Frequency Response Analysis (FRA) is a well-known technique used for power transformer condition monitoring for more than 40 years. Some research lines use this technique in other machines such as synchronous machines. This paper presents onsite tests on the field winding of a 125 MVA synchronous machine installed in a pumped storage power plant. The tests have been accomplished in standstill and rated speed conditions. The main contribution of this article is to demonstrate that the speed of the rotor has a significant influence on the field winding FRA test results. A comparison between standstill condition and rated speed FRA tests is presented. The frequency range where the differences take place indicates that centrifugal forces at rated speed change the capacitance of the field windings.

articleTitle: Diagnosis of Passing over Railway Joints and Reducing the Effects in Modern Traction Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: This paper analyses the possibility to diagnose the disturbances due to the passage of wheels over the rail joints in a traction system and offers a solution to diminish theirs effects. This is one of the specific phenomena of railway traction associated with a sudden variation of the load torque that can lead to unfavorable effects on the traction system. Diagnosing the direct effects and taking the appropriate decision to reduce the negative effects is not a practical solution, due to the rapidity with which the variations in the friction force occur. The only way to reduce or eliminate the negative effects is the use of a closed control system with an adequate structure. The rotor flux-oriented control of the induction motor is one of the most effective vector control techniques that can be applied with good performance in electric traction. The fundamentals of rotor flux-oriented control are first pointed out, followed by the synthetic presentation of the structure of the control system, when current control of the voltage source inverter is adopted. The assessment of the control system performance when the wheels pass over the rail joints is carried out based on a dedicated Matlab-Simulink model. It is illustrated that the response of the system is very good, with superior performance both when the passage of wheels over the rail joints occurs during acceleration and in steady-state operation.

articleTitle: Bearing fault detection in induction motors using the ROCOF and k-nearest neighbors algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: The actual tendency in electric systems for industrial and academic applications is to lead them to the smart systems philosophy. Nowadays, electronic instrumentation is an interesting area for researchers for electric motors’ control, monitoring, and maintenance purposes. Motor current signal analysis is one of the most used methods for fault detection in electric machines due to its noninvasive nature and the vast amount of information it contains; several techniques have been developed for bearing fault detection based on current signals, commonly through a spectrum analysis. Because of this, this paper proposes a methodology based on the rate of change of frequency estimation and a machine learning classifier (k-nearest neighbors). In this work, bearing ball damage and outer race damage scenarios were analyzed using the proposed method via the Digital Taylor-Fourier Transform, resulting in accuracy percentages of 97% and 94% for each case, respectively. That methodology does not require characterization supervised by a qualified person.

articleTitle: Broken bar detection on IM using ROCOF and decision tree
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: Nowadays, instrumentation plays a leading role in new tendencies like Industry 4.0, the Internet of Things, or cloud computing. Instrumentation applied to induction motors for fault detection seeks to streamline scheduled maintenance. Maintenance tasks are imperative to ensure the correct operation of the induction motors. Therefore, fault detection is a topic of interest for researchers. Several techniques for electric machine monitoring have been developed to solve problems inherent to induction motors. Some are commonly based on spectral analysis that requires identifying the characteristic fault components. This paper proposes a novel technique non-based on identifying fault components using the Rate Of Change of Frequency of current signals and a decision tree for broken squirrel-cage rotor bar detection under three load conditions: unloaded, 50%, and 75% of load. Provided results reported an accuracy of 100% for the three loading conditions and 2% of false positives for the half-loaded motor.

articleTitle: Drying out of a 11 kV-4900 kVA Synchronous Machine through Different Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: The moisture content is a critical parameter in the insulation of all the electrical machines, from oil-transformers to dry rotating machines. In the case of synchronous machines, drying out is a usual practice, especially hydro generators. In case of a low value of the insulation resistance or a low value of the polarization index the machine should be dried out. This paper presents the experience in drying out a 4900 kVA, 11 kV, brushless synchronous machine by two different methods.

articleTitle: IoT based Multi-Environmental Sensing System: Monitoring of Rotor Fault in Induction Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: This paper presents an IoT based multi-environmental sensing system in order to monitor the rotor bar fault in induction motors. For this purpose, an upgraded prototype all-in one smart sensor including vibration, flux and acoustic measures is built up and tested under rotor bar fault. The developed smart sensor has online and remote monitoring capabilities through IoT technology. The experimental results under different torque profiles shows that the rotor bar fault can be diagnosed and monitored accurately by utilizing IoT based multi-environmental sensing system which use the three-axes vibration, stray flux and acoustic data in induction motors.

articleTitle: Variable Speed Drives AC Ground Fault Location by Voltages Components Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: Variable Speed Drives (VSD) are key pieces in most of the industrial process. Its protection and diagnosis should be crucial in order to ensure the secure operation of VSDs especially against ground faults, the most common type of electrical faults. However, the transitions between AC and DC sides provoked by power electronics as well as the induced noises can cause the malfunction of protection relays. This paper proposed a method to locate ground faults in the AC output of a variable speed drive. The method is mainly based on a grounding resistor installed between the midpoint of the DC bus and ground. Measuring the phase-to-neutral voltages and grounding resistor voltage, the method can discern the faulty phase. Moreover, it estimates the fault position and fault resistance applying phasors equations with the fundamental and the commutation frequencies, no matters the inverter conditions or DC bus voltage. The method has been corroborated through computer simulations obtaining promising results in VSDs with floating supplies, which is a typical configuration for electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation of a High-Fidelity Transient Model for an Interior Permanent Magnet Machine with Arbitrary Stator Turn Fault
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: An accurate transient model of the machine operating under fault conditions is essential to save time and resources for experimental testing when developing fault-tolerant control strategies. This paper describes the LUT based simulation and experimental verification of the high-fidelity interior permanent magnet machine model with stator turn fault available in the literature. The approach involves the extraction of flux linkage maps of the machine under turn fault conditions using offline static finite element (FE) analysis,and combining it with voltage equations of the machine. The method is not limited to IPM machines and can be used to model stator turn faults in other machines such as surface PM machines, synchronous reluctance machines, switched reluctance machines, wound field synchronous machines, etc. The proposed approach provides a complete representation of the spatial harmonics and magnetic saturation in the presence of inter-turn faults and under all load conditions, making it the most accurate representation of the faulty motor behaviour apart from a time stepping FE coupled analysis.

articleTitle: Inspecting Static Frequency Converter Station with Thermography
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: Static Frequency Converter stations are becoming an important part of energy infrastructure. It is crucial to maintain their health and performance. One of versatile health indicators is temperature – many failure modes are associated with abnormal temperatures. As an operating station is off-limits to people, for safety reasons, it is important to be able to measure the temperatures at a distance. This paper describes measurements carried out at a small test Static Frequency Converter station using a hand-held thermal camera. Investigated equipment included valves, reactor coils, filter resistors, cooling system, joints, structure elements. The station was operating at rated voltage, but minimal power, therefore not all measurements were expected to be significant. Nevertheless, a number of anomalies has been detected, proving the usefulness of thermography in station diagnostics.

articleTitle: The Effects of Bearing Lubrication on Vibration, Acoustic and Stray Flux Signals in Induction Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: Rolling element bearings are among the most common and critical components in industrial rotating machinery. Lubrication on the rolling element bearing is critical to avoid machines from performance reduction and emergency shutdown. Less or over lubrication is one of the most essential reasons for decrease on rolling element bearing life. This paper focus on dynamic behaviors of vibration, acoustic, stray flux as well as frame temperature of induction motor for before and after bearing lubrication. For this purpose, rolling bearing lubrication is carried out and the corresponding signals are collected thorough a IoT based all-in-one smart sensor to analyze the vibration, acoustic and stray flux data. It is shown that rolling bearing lubrication has significantly affects the acoustics signal while there are some effective time and frequency range for vibration and stray flux.

articleTitle: Detection of Shaft Misalignment of a PMSM using Zoom-FFT
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: In this paper, Shaft Misalignment of a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) is investigated, through a computationally-efficient method, Zoom-FFT. Conventional FFT computes a wide-range frequency spectrum while only a part of the frequency spectrum is necessary for fault detection. As conventional Zoom-FFT may lead to higher complexity for narrow fault-related frequency bands, a Two Stage Zoom-FFT analysis has been proposed, which offers a low-complexity solution, taking advantage of the current measurement sensors integrated in the PMSM drive system. The proposed method has been validated through experimental testing under different operating conditions.

articleTitle: Development of a universal diagnostic system for stator winding faults of induction motor and PMSM based on transfer learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: This paper deals with the possibility of using transfer learning (TL) of a deep convolutional network (CNN) to develop a universal stator winding fault diagnostic system for the induction motor (IM) and the permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM). The proposed diagnostic system uses direct processing of phase current signals to detect and evaluate the degree of stator damage. The TL idea was based on using the CNN structure pre-trained for the IM diagnostic system in a diagnostic application dedicated to IM and PMSM. Experimental verification carried out on real objects confirmed very high precision of steady-state and transient damage detection and classification for both IM and PMSM. Furthermore, the detection time shown in the study for both types of machines did not exceed 0.07 seconds.

articleTitle: Thermal management of electrically excited synchronous motor with integrated thermal network in automotive drive system
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: The trend toward vehicle electrification brings new opportunities and challenges for various types of electric machines, such as electrically excited synchronous motor (EESM). In EESM, rotor currents are required to create flux linkage. Adjustable rotor current adds a third degree of freedom to control the EESM. However, the rotor current also creates losses that can lead to critical temperatures. To take advantage of this degree of freedom and to balance the thermal states between the stator and the rotor, a new concept of EESM thermal management is presented in this paper, which aims to reduce the temperature increase during overheating. First, a low-order lumped-parameter thermal network (LPTN) is generated for temperature monitoring. Based on the thermal network, the control algorithm balances the temperatures of the stator and the rotor to slow down the temperature increase in the critical part. A simplified automotive drive system was built to simulate this control strategy. The SFTP-US06 drive cycle was used in the drive system to validate the control strategy.

articleTitle: Radial Lumped-parameter Model of a Ball Bearing for Simulated Fault Signatures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: In the literature, lumped-parameter models of ball bearing have been widely developed to provide vibration data for condition monitoring purposes. These are generic models which consider the contacts occurring between the two rings and all the balls in the bearing thanks to Hertzian contact stress theory. In this paper, a radial lumped-parameter model is developed on MATLAB/Simulink for a single ball in contact with the bearing races under a load distribution as a function of its angular position on the races. This simplified radial model identifies fault signatures in frequency domain for inner and outer ring defects. Afterward, the model is evaluated in contrast with the experimental data for OR faults provided by the Case Western Reserve University open-source dataset. The radial lumped- parameter model is able to reproduce the fault signatures for the same working conditions as the experimental data for OR defects of several geometries.

articleTitle: Artificial intelligence (AI)-based optimization of power electronic converters for improved power system stability and performance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: The present review paper provides an overview of the recent advances in AI-based techniques for the design and optimization of power electronic converters. There is an increased demand on power converters in applications like renewable energy generation, microgrids, electric and hybrid vehicles, high-voltage DC power transmission etc. with focus on their design and optimization. In this context, various AI techniques are discussed, such as: machine learning, deep learning, reinforcement learning, and evolutionary algorithms, artificial neural networks, fuzzy logic control, expert systems and their applications in power electronics and electric drives. Some case studies from the literature are referred and potential benefits of AI-assisted design and optimization of power electronic converters with aspects of enhanced power system stability and performance are highlighted.

articleTitle: Motor Eccentricity Fault Detection: Physics-Based and Data-Driven Approaches
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: Fault detection using motor current signature analysis (MCSA) is attractive for industrial applications due to its simplicity with no additional sensor installation required. However current components associated with faults are often very subtle and much smaller than the supply frequency component, making it challenging to detect and quantify fault levels. In this paper, we present our work on quantitative eccentricity fault diagnosis technologies for electric motors, including physical-model approach using improved winding function theory, which can simulate motor dynamics under faulty conditions and agrees well with experiment data, and data-driven approach using topological data analysis (TDA), which can effectively differentiate signals measured at different eccentricity levels. The advantages and limitations of each approach is discussed. Both methods can be extended to the detection and quantification of other types of electric motor faults.

articleTitle: Detection of Shorted Turns in the Field Winding of Turbo Generators during Turning Gear Mode
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: A new test method for detecting shorted turns in the field winding of synchronous generators during turning gear mode operation is proposed in this paper. Turbo generators are operated in turning gear mode, where the rotor is turned at low speed (0-50 rpm), after shutdown or before startup to prevent thermal bowing of the turbine and generator rotor. The main idea of the new test method is to test the rotor field winding condition from the stator winding side by observing the change in the equivalent impedance as a function of rotor position while the rotor is rotated slowly. The decrease in the d-axis impedance due to shorted turns in the field winding is observed for fault detection with high sensitivity. It is shown that the proposed method provides a simple and convenient means of testing shorted field turns with high sensitivity and reliability compared to existing off-line and on-line test methods. The validity of the proposed method that has not been attempted elsewhere, is verified on 4 pole, 20 kVA and 2 pole, 5.5 kVA synchronous machines.

articleTitle: Broadband Technique Analysis for Insulation Fault Detection and Condition Monitoring in Rotating Electrical Machines
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive discussion and review of cutting-edge techniques for insulation diagnosis and monitoring in rotating electrical machines, using broadband electrical excitation. These techniques cover a frequency range from a few kHz to the MHz band and are classified into three categories. Firstly, the paper explores the application of Frequency Response Analysis (FRA) to rotating machines. Secondly, techniques based on parasitic capacitance and Common-mode (CM) broadband impedance tracking are discussed. Finally, the paper examines methodologies related to high-frequency oscillations in the phase current following a switching event.

articleTitle: Comparison of high frequency winding modeling for stator health monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: The purpose of machine stator health monitoring is to follow up the evolution of the insulation with aging. In this context, this paper focuses on the high-frequency equivalent models often used to ensure this monitoring. The most representative models of real high frequency behavior will be presented. After a comparative study of these models and their representability, we will present our proposal for a high frequency monitoring method. This last one is based on a numerical characterization of the stator admittance.

articleTitle: Bayesian Experiment Design for the Development of an Epoxy Resin Degradation Model
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to design of highly time-consuming aging experiments of electrical insulation system (EIS) materials, specifically epoxy resin, through Bayesian methods. The aim is to find a suitable model with as few experiments as possible. This is achieved by evaluation the information gain for each potential new experimental condition, and select the most informative conditions for measurement. If a model structure is not entirely known, multiple candidate models can be designed and the experiment design procedure quickly discriminates between them. The method is compared with the conventional approach of factorial experiment design and Response Surface Methodology (RMS). The aging of the epoxy samples is then hygrothermal, using temperature and humidity as two factors. This aging setup is not well studied, as the experiments are very demanding, but of high importance for the diagnostics of electrical machines. The results then show that the Bayesian approach is able to find models whose predictions match the validation measurement better than conventional methods.

articleTitle: Fault Tolerance Analysis of Multiphase Ironless PMSM for Flywheel Batteries
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: This paper investigates the performances of an Ironless PMSM with two phase faults: open circuit of a phase and short circuit of a phase. The machine was specifically designed for a Flywheel Energy Storage System (FESS) and is reconfigurable as 3-Phase, 6-Phase and 12-Phase. The machine is meant to be used in domestic applications with a photovoltaic panel and grid connectsion. The performances of each multiphase configuration under faulty and healhty conditions are compared on the basis of annual energy savings, in order to state the optimal configuration for fault toleance.

articleTitle: Stator Imbalance in Asymmetrical Six-Phase Synchronous Motor Drives: High-Resistance Connections and Mismanufactured Winding
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: An electric drive can experience a wide variety of faults. Some of them, such as short circuits, can significantly harm the structural integrity of the drive. Others, such as poor connections or manufacturing asymmetries in the stator winding, might not affect the drive integrity but distort the electrical quantities (voltages and currents), causing overheating and imbalances. Improper connections could lead to resistance imbalance, while bad manufacturing may result in some phases having fewer or more turns than expected at the design stage. An analytical approach based on the Vector-Space Decomposition (VSD) is proposed in this paper to model the imbalance resulting from High-Resistance Connections (HRCs) or Manufacturing Defects (MDs) due to a variation in the number of turns.The study is carried out for a six-phase surface-mounted permanent magnet (SMPM) brushless motor, but it may be extended to any multi-three-phase drive. Finite-element simulations are used to build a realistic model of the electrical machine and confirm the theoretical outcomes.

articleTitle: Inline solution for characterization of chip substrate connections by Laser Speckle Photometry
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: In the production of power electronics, quality, and reliability is an important factor. Especially, the connection layer between the chip and the ceramic based substrate often includes defects which can reduce the heat dissipation in these areas. This can lead to overheating and furthermore reduce the lifetime of the component. In the worst case, failures like this can have a huge impact on safety relevant systems. Therefore, a quality control within the production line or at least before the packaging of the components is very important.The Laser Speckle Photometry (LSP) provides a promising solution to this problem. Speckle patterns are generated by interfering light waves that are reflected by the illuminated surface.In this paper, a quality control concept based on the LSP in the production process of power electronic chips for the automotive industry is presented. The aim is to find and evaluate the voids in the solder connection, and furthermore determine the porosity in sintered connections. Especially, the size and location of these voids are of great interest. First investigations have shown promising results, finding defects with the size of less than 15 % (v/v) of the actual connection layer of the chips. This proves that the LSP has a big potential to inspect the connection quality of chips during the manufacturing of power electronics.

articleTitle: Optimised Online Multi-Sine Battery Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy using a Three-Phase Neutral Point Clamped Converter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) is a method that is commonly used for determining the state of charge and state of health of batteries and fuel cells. Historically, it was used offline in research laboratories, but the rapid increase of demand for fuel cells and battery storage to meet the accelerating growth of electric vehicles and renewable energy has stimulated research into online in-situ EIS. This paper presents an online EIS technique integrated within the control and measurement system of a neutral point clamped (NPC) inverter. This is achieved by adding zero-sequence perturbation voltages to the inverter’s reference three phase voltages. By connecting the battery midpoint to the neutral point of the inverter, a perturbation current flows into the battery. Measurement of the battery voltage and current and subsequent spectral analysis are used to calculate its impedance. To speed up the EIS measurement, the perturbation signal includes multiple sinewaves of 5 different frequencies, instead of a single frequency sinewave. Furthermore, the phase angles of the sinewaves are optimised to prevent inverter overmodulation thus preventing distortion of the inverter’s output voltage. Detailed simulation results show close alignment of the proposed EIS measurement with theoretical values in the range of 0.01 Hz – 4 kHz, which covers the typical range for batteries and fuel cells’ interest frequency on the spectrum.

articleTitle: Investigation of Empirical Start-Up Strategy for Industrial Generator Through Vibration Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: In industrial environments, all machine components (rotor, stator, bearings, shaft), work under less-than-ideal conditions and, as a result, are subjected to degradation and eventual failure. Bearings are typically associated with more frequent faults, while being relatively easy to replace. Most bearing-related faults produce distinct vibrations and noise, thus facilitate local detection. This work investigates intense vibrations produced during a large synchronous generator start-up, while normal load operation remains in safe limits. Data from warm start-up of a power station is examined, and conclusions are drawn based on relative and absolute vibration patterns, produced during three different start-up modes. The results indicate the correct start-up procedure of this particular generator and how the operation inside the critical speed zones affects the alarms and trips.

articleTitle: A Novel Method for Rotor Fault Diagnostics in Induction Motors using Harmonic Isolation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: This paper presents a novel methodology for the detection and diagnosis of rotor faults in induction machines using signal estimation. The proposed approach is independent from the motor slip and relies on the isolation of main harmonics rather than on the investigation of signatures with traditional approaches such as the identification of fault-related sidebands. The method is applied on the stator line current capturing the transient nature of fault-related frequencies at the steady state. Thus, it enables a reliable diagnostic strategy by the isolated harmonics and their analysis over the time and frequency. The method’s effectiveness was explored with electromagnetic simulations of two induction machines of different geometry, manufacture, and power scale. Then, the method was validated experimentally on a 1.1 kW induction motor.

articleTitle: Online system identification and excitation for thermal monitoring of electric machines using machine learning and model predictive control
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: Data-driven thermal models are demonstrated to be practical for real-time temperature estimation in electric drive applications. However, the model’s performance and scope are highly influenced by the information contained in the empirical dataset. So far, thermal modeling and system excitation are separate processes where the system is excited using offline-designed, open-loop experiments that do not consider the system or model responses. This typically requires lengthy experimental measurement sessions at test benches and the missing feedback for the excitation leads to biased data distributions in the state-input space. To overcome these issues, model predictive based closed-loop system excitation is introduced, which identifies a neural network-based thermal model online using the continual data stream. Simulation results show that a significantly improved state-input dataset distribution can be achieved with the proposed solution in less time than traditional open-loop offline design of experiment strategies.

articleTitle: Thermal Degradation Profile of Concentrated Stator Winding Insulation by Impedance Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: Impedance spectroscopy is one of the continuously developing tools deployed for the inspection and evaluation of the health condition of electrical machines and machine components. Being a practical implementation and expansion of the Broadband Dielectric Spectroscopy (BDS) and the Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS), it allows the characterization of components by their amplitude and phase responses over frequency and the system’s resonances. To this direction, this paper presents a study on the effect of thermal degradation on the insulation system of concentrated stator coils from the stator winding of a 2MW permanent magnet synchronous generator purposed for aerospace applications. The thermal aging pattern and degradation mechanisms of the coil insulation are discussed through experimental results by ex-situ impedance spectroscopy.

articleTitle: Broken rotor bar fault detection using odd triple harmonics in delta-connected induction motors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: This paper aims to use and explore odd triple harmonics to perform fault detection in delta-connected induction motors, demonstrating their suitability to detect broken rotor bar. Harmonic components arise around the main odd triple components, generated by the interaction of the fault and other effects, as saturation and voltage unbalance. The paper presents the mathematical modeling introducing the harmonic components, along with experimental results under several load levels and voltage unbalances, demonstrating the performance of the odd triple harmonics. The results compare line and phase currents, demonstrating that the proposed harmonics perform satisfactorily in phase current, suitable for fault detection in a wide operational range, including low-load cases.

articleTitle: A Time-Frequency Analysis for Broken Rotor Bar Detection in Closed Loop Inverter Fed Induction Motor at Imposed Speed
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: In this paper, an analysis to detect broken rotor bars while the motor is operating in closed loop control is presented. Due to changes in the supply frequency, which occur to keep the speed constant, a time-frequency technique is required even when the transient is completed. Signals from the phase current of the induction motor are analysed using traditional methods such as the Fast Fourier Transform and the Short Time Fourier Transform. Finally, the same signals are analysed through the Dragon Transform, that ensures high resolution frequency and time and allows to detect trajectories of the harmonics with different load conditions.

articleTitle: Digital and wireless Operating Deflection Shape (ODS) for assets condition monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: The maintenance of industrial assets is responsible for a large part of the costs of an industrial plant. In this context, low-cost sensors were developed to measure physical quantities and enable online monitoring of assets. Most of these sensors use vibration measurements as a method for detecting and diagnosing faults or behavior deviations. This paper shows a method for using the Operating Deflection Shape (ODS) vibration signal analysis technique in conjunction with low-cost wireless condition monitoring IoT sensors. The developed method was confronted with commercial devices that perform traditional ODS, thus, laboratory and field validations are presented.

articleTitle: Contribution to a review of lithium-ion batteries diagnostic methods for space applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: Thanks to their excellent performance, lithium-ion batteries have become increasingly used in terrestrial and space applications. Despite the long lifespan, this type of battery is subject to inevitable aging dependent on electrochemical degradation phenomena. Defining a diagnostic method capable of estimating the state of health of a battery and predicting its end of life is therefore a priority to ensure proper functioning. Although considerable progress has been made in recent years in this research topic, most of the effort of the scientific community is concentrated in terrestrial applications. Of all the various existing approaches, both experimental and numerical, few are applicable within the limitations imposed by space applications. Hence, the main contribution of this paper is to provide an overview of the current state of the diagnostic methods adopted to estimate the aging of lithium-ion batteries used in satellites.

articleTitle: Data Generation Method for Domain Adaptation in Fault Diagnosis Using Motor Current Signals
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: Recently, the demand for data-driven fault diagnosis using motor current signals has increased, however, collecting labeled abnormal data in actual environments is difficult. We proposed a method to generate current signal data by combining simulation data, generated using the multiple coupled circuits model, with normal real data. The data are combined using frequency and phase matching and data assimilation. Our proposed method can reproduce more diverse features than conventional methods and enables more domain-invariant features to be learned by sim-to-real domain adaptation. We evaluated the proposed and conventional data generation methods on the task of classifying the number of broken rotor bars in an induction machine using five unsupervised domain adaptation algorithms. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperformed all conventional methods with respect to classification accuracy. This study was the first to adopt sim-to-real domain adaptation for current-signal-based fault diagnosis.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Analysis of Line-Start Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines with Explosion-Proof Capability in Explosive Atmospheres: Reviewing Standards and Guidelines
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: With the growing demand for higher energy efficiency and safety in explosive (Ex) atmospheres, there is a high potential to use line-start permanent magnet synchronous machines (LS-PMSMs) in such areas as in various other industrial applications. However, to ensure high-energy efficient LS-PMSM's safe and effective operation in potentially explosive atmospheres (hazardous locations), it is crucial to comply with the relevant standards and guidelines. Therefore, the analysis highlights the need for compliance with the relevant standards and guidelines to ensure the safe and efficient operation of LS-PMSMs in hazardous locations. This paper primarily focuses on the analysis of LS-PMSMs through various experimental tests, which are conducted following relevant standards. The objective is to ensure the enhanced safety of LS-PMSMs and explore their potential use in hazardous locations and for future advancements in test methods. The findings of this paper can be useful for researchers, engineers, and professionals involved in the design, installation, and operation of LS-PMSMs in hazardous locations.

articleTitle: Diagnostics of a double-cage induction motor under steady state with the rotor asymmetry
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: This article presents a method of diagnosing the rotor circuits of a double-cage induction motor operating under a steady state at a constant angular velocity. A circuit model of the motor is formulated, considering an infinite spectrum of spatial harmonics in the airgap under the parametric asymmetry of the rotor cages. This facilitates the qualitative determination of diagnostic signals in the phase current of the stator circuit. The proposed method can effectively recognize the location and level of damage. The harmonic balance method is used to solve the model. Example calculations are provided for a medium power motor, associated in a star without a neutral conductor and a rotor shorted using separate rings.

articleTitle: Comparison of Demagnetization Behavior of Radial and Halbach Array PMs in Fault-Tolerant Synchronous Machines Operating with Open Phases
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study of the demagnetization behavior of permanent magnets arranged in the radial and Halbach array directions during the operation of fault-tolerant permanent magnet synchronous machines with open phases. Finite element analysis has shown that Halbach array permanent magnet synchronous machines with open slots offer the highest power density, have higher losses in permanent magnets and provide worse demagnetization picture at high temperatures in permanent magnets. In contrast, the machines with radially arranged permanent magnets and semi-closed slots generate higher losses in the stator winding, lower losses in permanent magnets, and provide a better demagnetization picture at high temperatures in permanent magnets, in comparison to the Halbach array machine. Finally, radially arranged permanent magnets have better demagnetization picture during short-time overcurrent in the stator winding, supplied by the converter.
