articleTitle: Fault Harmonics Current Detection in Closed-loop Controlled Induction Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: Inverters are used to supply induction motors in the industry and electric traction. Inverters can operate in open-loop or closed-loop control. This work aims to study how the control mode affects fault detection and observation in the stator current spectrum of winding and rotor slot harmonics. We present an experimental study on these effects. In closed-loop control, the steady-state analysis of the stator current with the Fourier transform is unsuitable due to slight variations in the motor speed and the supply voltage frequency. It is necessary to use a time-frequency analysis technique. In this case, the short-time Fourier transform is used, which is well adapted to slow speed and frequency variations. It allows observing the trajectory in the time-frequency plane of the fault, winding and rotor slot harmonics.

articleTitle: Getting the Most Out of the Pole Drop Test for Detecting Rotor Faults in Salient Pole Synchronous Machines
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: The pole drop test is the most common test applied for detecting shorted turns in the field winding of salient pole synchronous machines (SM). It is a simple off-line test where ac voltage is applied to the field winding, and the asymmetric voltage drop between poles is used as an indicator of shorted turns. However, it is known to have significant risk of giving false indications due to imperfections or defects in the windings, pole, or airgap distribution. Although the test has been applied extensively in the field, the research conducted on the topic is limited. In this paper, new guidelines on testing and interpretation of the pole drop test for improving the sensitivity and reliability of fault detection are presented. An analysis shows that the performance of the test is influenced by the test conditions (rotor in/out, ac/dc voltage) and fault indicator used. Based on the analysis, an insight into how the pole drop test can be performed and interpreted for detecting and classifying field winding, damper bar, and eccentricity faults with maximum sensitivity is provided for improving the reliability of SM fault detection. Experimental results on 5.5 and 30 kVA salient pole SMs are given to support the claims made.

articleTitle: Automatic detection of corrosion in ball bearings of soft-started induction motors, obtaining the persistence spectrum of the stray-flux signals
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: This work, presents a novel method to automatically detect and classify the presence of corrosion in ball bearings of soft-started induction motors. The method relies, first, in obtaining the persistence spectrum images of the part of the stray-flux signals in which the soft-starter is in operation. Then, those images are used as input for a convolutional neural network, which automatically differentiates not only between healthy or faulty bearings, but also between different levels of corrosion in the ball bearings. For the study, a soft-starter of a well-known brand is used to start an induction motor, setting different combinations of the variable parameters of that device. Also, different levels of load are applied to the motor. The proposed method proves its potential, achieving a high accuracy.

articleTitle: The Stator Current Spectrum as Fault Identification Mean for Combined Faults in an AFPM Synchronous Generator
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: The article investigates the stator current spectrum of the machine, as fault identification mean in the cases of partial demagnetization, and partial demagnetization combined with static eccentricity, either angular or axis. The machine in which the analysis had been done is an Axial Flux Permanent Magnet (AFPM) Synchronous Generator, with double-sided rotor topology and a coreless stator. The generator's healthy and faulty simulations are conducted using Finite Element Method (FEM) in three dimensions. The novelty of this article is that, although the stator current spectrum had been widely used as a fault identification mean in electrical machines with conventional topology, it is used for the first time for combined fault analysis in AFPM synchronous machines.

articleTitle: Online Stator Fault Diagnostics and Performance Comparison of Stator Winding Configurations in Symmetrical Six-Phase Induction Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: Multiphase machines provide various significant benefits when compared to three-phase ones. Their most alluring quality is frequently thought to be their innate forgiveness of flaws. The Inter-Turn Short Circuit Fault (ITSCF) is among the potential failure types that are particularly frequent. As opposed to this, multiphase machines with symmetrical winding arrangements provide a variety of options for stator winding configurations. In this study, the symmetrical six-phase induction motor (6SPIM) was controlled by a model predictive control (MPC) algorithm, an attractive control scheme for the regulation of multiphase electric drives since it easily exploits their inherent advantages. The proposed indicators, which are based on the stator’s voltages and currents’ symmetrical components ratio, offer reduced calculations, are non-invasive, and are a relatively affordable budget solution. Using the stator’s windings, impedances are estimated from the magnitudes of the fundamental spectrum component of both current and voltage signals measured using the Short Time Least Square Prony’s (STLSP) method. The work was validated using experimental results, taking into consideration different operating conditions and the different types of stator winding configurations (double star, double delta, and hexagon connection).

Author Keywords: Short Time Least Square Prony’s Method (STLSP)

articleTitle: Study of thermo-oxidative ageing applied to an epoxy resin using a microstrip ring resonator structure
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: Dielectric material ageing is one of the main issues which induces electrical machine failure. This ageing is most generally induced by thermal and electrical stresses, oxidation, or a combination of these different effects. Ultra-High Frequency (300 MHz - 3 GHz) characterization may be a promising method for the insulation ageing assessment, by monitoring the evolution of the dielectric properties in this frequency band. This characterization can be performed using electromagnetic sensors. Therefore, the main topic of this study focuses on the relative permittivity evolution of epoxy resin samples exposed to thermo-oxidative stress measured by a microstrip ring resonator. The first step is to determine if the sensitivity of this sensor is sufficient to identify a change in the dielectric properties of the resin samples. In order to correlate these potential changes induced by ageing phenomena, Fouriertransform infrared spectroscopy and mass loss measurements are also performed.

articleTitle: Detection of Trailing-Edge Demagnetization for Six-Phase Permanent Magnet Motors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: The trailing edge demagnetization in Surface-Mounted Permanent-Magnet Synchronous Motors (SMPMSMs) is commonly the result of an excessive torque overload. This fault irreversibly reduces the torque constant and motor efficiency, and it is often difficult to diagnose in three-phase machines for small demagnetization angles. Conversely, multiphase drives providing additional degrees of freedom make it possible to develop new potential diagnostic algorithms that are more accurate and robustThis paper proposes a diagnostic algorithm for the online detection of rotor demagnetization faults for six-phase machines with parallel magnetized rotor magnets. The proposed technique directly quantifies the demagnetization angle and actively corrects the angular position of the control system to ensure maximum motor performance in post-fault conditions. Experimental tests have been carried out on two identical six-phase PMSMs differing only in the size of the rotor magnets to emulate the effect of a trailing edge demagnetization. The experimental results confirm the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed solution.

articleTitle: Motor Current Signal Analysis for the Diagnostics of Localized Bearing Defects
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: This paper discusses the detection of a single point bearing defect in an induction machine using the motor current signature analysis in an induction machine. The idea is to understand the relation between the detection of such faults, the link between mechanical vibrations and radial displacement of the shaft caused by the faults, the sensitivity of detecting the fault based on a magnetic circuit analysis leading to its reflection on stator current. The impact of some of the other parameters related to machine design and bearing design is also discussed. Finally, the paper is concluded by discussing how motor current signature analysis (MCSA) can assist the diagnostics or prognostics.

articleTitle: Mechanical Fault Detection in Induction Motors Using a Feature-Based Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: In this paper, a data-driven algorithm to identify the eccentricity fault in induction motors is proposed. The algorithm is based on the Kalman Filter (KF) and utilizes experimental data collected from healthy and faulty three-phase stator currents at different speeds and load conditions. Additional data processing techniques including Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT), Power Spectral Density (PSD), and cepstrum are used to extend the dataset. A feature extraction process involving a few statistical measures is applied to this dataset. For each feature, a State-Space Model (SSM) and a KF are formulated. By comparing the resulting output of the SSMs with the estimated output from KFs, a measure to identify an eccentricity fault is obtained. This method was tested on various operating modes of an induction motor, demonstrating its effectiveness in distinguishing healthy data from those indicating an eccentricity fault.

articleTitle: Investigation of Changes in Partial Discharge Properties of Insulation Material over Lifetime under Accelerated Aging Conditions
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: Machines fed by inverters are stressed by high dv/dt as well as high switching frequencies. With the introduction of power switches, based on wide bandgap technology like silicon carbide (SiC) technology dv/dt as well as switching frequencies are again significantly increased. With the application of SiC inverters into industrial applications, lifetime considerations of insulation material become critical. At the same time there are almost no investigations and very few literature available, on the reaction of insulation materials to this new boundary conditions. Primary electrical degradation mechanism of insulation material is partial discharge (PD) and international standards define repetitive partial discharge inception voltage (RPDIV) as well as repetitive partial discharge extinction voltage (RPDEV) as one of the key parameters for characterizing electrical stress and resistance of materials to this electrical stress. In this paper the parameters RPDIV/RPDEV characterizing the partial discharge properties as well as their development over lifetime of the material are investigated under accelerated aging conditions. Specimen of insulation material used in form wound windings is stressed beyond specification to reduce lifetime and thus test durations. Pulse voltage stress is applied bipolar under defined frequency and duty cycle. Aging is periodically interrupted to perform RPDIV/RPDEV tests. As a result, it is possible to trace these parameters over lifetime, depending on the stress level applied. While the overall lifetime shows a clear and well-known trend with increasing stress level, the observed trend in PD properties over lifetime obviously change depending on stress level.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach for Early Detection of Inter-turn Faults in Induction Motors during Start-up
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: Early inter-turn faults (ITFs) are one of the most challenging and important faults to detect due to their rapid evolution into a catastrophic stator failure, which, in turn, is one of the main reasons for motor failures in medium and high-voltage induction motors (IMs). Despite all this, there is an under-representation of this topic in the technical literature. This under-representation is even more significant when it comes to transient analysis. Yet, today’s computer capabilities open up the possibility of filling this gap through the combined use of finite element software (as safe test-benches to study the fault) and powerful time-frequency tools. This paper aims to contribute to this gap by thoroughly investigating the diagnosis of early-stage ITFs during IM start-up. The first part of the work conducts a deep finite element analysis of three motors of different characteristics that leads to discovering and fully characterizing a family of ITFs-related harmonics not described before in previous literature. Finally, their existence is proven in a 0.75 kW IM through a novel methodology that emulates the electromagnetic effects of an ITF but without endangering the stator’s windings.

articleTitle: Search Coil Based Detection of the Inter-Turn Short Circuits in Aircraft Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine by Signal Frequency Extraction
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: This paper demonstrates a new methodology towards the reliable detection of the inter-turn short circuits in surface-mounted permanent magnet synchronous machines specially designed for aviation applications. The diagnostic strategy deploys search coil based condition monitoring in conjunction with a frequency extraction algorithm for the detection and evaluation of stator fault-related harmonics. The discussed approach is investigated on a 42 kW PM machine, with a double layer tooth coil winding with the help of Finite Element simulations. The impact of the inter-turn fault is investigated at different operating conditions, notably rotational speed and PWM frequencies, thus enabling the investigation and identification of harmonics that show compelling diagnostic potential for detecting the fault even at incipient severity levels.

articleTitle: Perspectives of Transfer Learning on the Diagnosis of Faults in Electrical Machines, Power Electronics, and Drives
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: Fault Diagnosis and Failure Prognosis on Electrical Machines, Drives, and Power Electronics has seen rapid advancement in the last decades. Nevertheless, there is a pressing need for rapid and data efficient training of algorithms that can be applied across platforms and under varying operating conditions and environments. Contemporary machine learning methods based on transfer learning and semantic consistent identification techniques have found wide acceptance in the processing of audio, video and other applications, while requiring minimal training. This review discusses the available techniques and the applications to-date to the diagnosis and identification of faults, and failure prognosis.

articleTitle: A Projection-Based Support Vector Machine Algorithm for Induction Motors’ Bearing Fault Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: This paper proposes a binary fault detection algorithm for detecting inner raceway bearing faults in a 4KW induction motor. The algorithm uses Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Projection Recurrent Neural Network (PRNN) techniques and is based on data collected experimentally at different speeds and load conditions. Time and frequency contents of the three-phase stator currents are analysed using Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT), Power Spectral Density (PSD), and cepstrum analysis. A feature set is obtained using various statistical measures, and feature selection algorithms are used to select the most relevant features. The SVM is then trained using these features, and its optimisation problem is formulated as Constrained Nonlinear Programming (NCP). A PRNN is proposed to solve the NCP and obtain the optimal decision boundary of the SVM. The study demonstrates that the accuracy of the algorithm depends on the type of kernel function and the number of relevant features selected. The results suggest that the proposed algorithm is effective in detecting inner raceway bearing faults in induction motors.

articleTitle: Classification of Bearing Faults in Induction Motors with the Hilbert-Huang Transform and Feature Selection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: This study proposes a novel approach to detect bearing damage in induction motors during operation. Vibration signals from the Case Western Reserve University dataset of bearings are used to validate this proposal. The data are preprocessed using the Hilbert-Huang transform, and 10 attributes are extracted from both the time and time-frequency domains. Synthetic minority oversampling technique (SMOTE) is applied to remove imbalances in the dataset, the random forest (RF) as a feature selection extractor and the variance inflation factor (VIF) are used to select the proper features for good performance in fault identification. Grid search is employed to find the optimal parameters of five well-known supervised machine learning algorithms to classify two scenarios: i) health and fault bearing, and ii) health and types of bearing faults. The results show that k-nearest neighbor (k-NN) and RF are the most suitable classifiers, with accuracies of 99.7% and 89.34%, respectively.

articleTitle: Estimation of Torque Sharing for Industrial Dual Induction Motor Drives under Special Current Sensor Configuration
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: Industrial electronic control units used in three-phase single-motor AC drives typically present three input channels conceived to read the stator current vector. Usually, two current sensors are placed at the inverter output and serve to compute a motor torque and flux upon which drive is controlled. However, to increase interchangeability, control units are utilised indistinctly for the control of single-motor and parallel-connected multi-motor drives. When multiple motors are supplied by a single inverter, the current sensors deliver the sum of the phase stator current of all motors. If load imbalances arise, drive might go under asymmetrical heating, producing imprecise torque and worsening dynamic response. Specially under load imbalances, it is useful to know the torque sharing, since it can be used to enhance drive performance. In this paper, the torque sharing of dual induction motors is computed under a special current sensor configuration that uses three current sensors. A comparison of several signal processing schemes is presented. Experimental results measured on a dual induction motor test bench show the ability and precision of the proposed schemes to compute the torque and flux of each individual motor.

articleTitle: Speed and Torque Estimation in Induction Motor through the Analysis of Stray Flux Signals
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: Induction motors are elements of great importance within the industry due to the large number of applications they have; because of this, their monitoring is essential to ensure the correct performance of the tasks. Several methods have been created for the estimation of speed and torque in these machines, many of these methods use sensors that are invasive to the motor or require taking it off-line to perform a series of tests to obtain the necessary parameters for its estimation. The present research proposes a methodology for the estimation of speed and torque in induction motors through the analysis of stray flux signals obtained in a non-invasive manner and the information provided by the manufacturer on the data plate of the machine. Preliminary results show a speed estimation with an error of less than 0.2% and a methodological proposal for torque estimation, as well as clear prospectives to improve the methodology to obtain better results in torque estimation and to generalize the method by testing the algorithm with different machines.

articleTitle: Influence of Battery Aging on Converter Switching Device Degradation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: In this work, a methodology to examine the influence of battery degradation on the converter semiconductor switching devices is presented. A PV-battery case study is used to demonstrate the methodology and show possible results. Initially, the results indicate a very limited influence of the battery on converter lifetime of 1 %. This is due to counteracting effects during battery degradation, which both decreases the power flow through the converter but increases the losses. A second simulation with constant power flow, isolating the effect of the reduced energy flow, showed an 9 % converter lifetime decrease using a degrading battery, demonstrating the underlying effect. The paper shows the battery model, converter model and case study results including battery degradation profiles, converter losses and reliability distributions.

articleTitle: Performance of Machine-Learning-Based Algorithms for Anomaly Detection in Variable Frequency Drives Using Temperature Signals
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: Smart condition-based maintenance is an essence of Industry 4.0 and is important for assuring independent and long-term operation of devices driven by Variable Frequency Drives (VFD). Therefore, detection of early-stage signs of fatigue and failures in VFDs is important. This usually involves analysis of input data, extracted from VFDs and external sensors, using temperature, vibration, and acoustic signals, among others. Nevertheless, due to the complexity of operation of VFDs, there is a constant need to define more unified approaches for detecting anomalies in their operation, so that higher performance and reliability can be achieved. In this paper, we present a comparative study on machine-learning based solutions, utilizing temperature signals, fetched from both real and simulated operation of VFDs in wind turbine and virtual drive, respectively. This involved Hidden Markov Models, Deep Autoencoders, and Incremental/Kernel Principal Component Analysis. We also introduced a novel anomaly metric, so that all the approaches could be efficiently benchmarked in terms of sensitivity to anomalies of distinct types. Our study confirms the feasibility of the methods in both real and simulated data from VFDs. This proves that machine-learning-based methodologies can be successfully applied for condition monitoring, via anomaly detection, in VFDs.

articleTitle: Implementation of Likelihood of Failure (LoF) Methodology for HV Motors in Industry
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: Induction motors are widely used in the industry as an electrical driver. Unavailability of the motors due to failure can negatively impact the production and safety of a facility. Some failures can be avoided by identifying the inception of faults via condition monitoring methods. This allows preventive action to be taken to avoid continuous deterioration of the motor in operation up to a point of failure. Condition based monitoring also allows us to move from the conventional time-based maintenance approach towards risk-based maintenance. This paper describes the likelihood of failure methodology adopted from a string of electrical tests and further enhanced to include maintenance and operation records of the motor. The LoF was applied to 65 machines across our assets as a tool to assess and evaluate the risk involved in deciding if the motor is required to be removed from service for inspection or overhaul. Test records for 2 motors are summarized and the corresponding LoF is further discussed in the case study section. Based on the analysis of the sample, the LoF methodology can be further improved by supplementing real time data from motor sensors such as current and winding temperature as both these parameters can directly impact insulation life. Digitalizing and integrating these offline and online data onto a single platform will contribute to higher confidence level and provide a more dynamic overview of our motor condition.

articleTitle: Transformerless Wind Energy System Based on a Series Double NPC Multilevel Rectifier and a Six-Phase Asymmetrical PMSG
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: This paper introduces a transformerless configuration of generator and power converter that is suitable for offshore wind energy systems. The proposed configuration is based on a series connection of two neutral point clamped (NPC) multilevel rectifiers, powered by a six-phase asymmetrical permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG). Additionally, this work proposes a control strategy that opens the door to a fault-tolerance mode, by the use of independent controllers for each NPC converter, directly operating in a large-signal nonlinear space. This closed-loop system permits to prevent disruptions due to faults at either the generator winding or one of the NPC converter, by allowing a modular modification of set-points over the whole system operating region. Simulation results show the feasibility of the proposed configuration, rendering a promising solution for future wind energy generation systems.

articleTitle: Insights on diagnostic signals in single-phase and three-phase induction motors in single-phasing fault
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: The aim of this paper is twofold. On the one hand, the applicability of the well-known diagnostic techniques, based on the motor current and stray flux signature analysis, has been experimentally tested both on small single-phase induction motors and on large on-field three-phase induction motors. On the other hand, the single phasing fault in three-phase induction motors, which has rarely been treated in the literature, has been experimentally analyzed and compared to the behavior of the single-phase motor, in order to find characteristic signatures of this fault. Time and frequency domain analyses were performed on current, axial and radial stray flux, and torque signals. The experimental study highlighted the following insights: i) classical motor current signature analysis cannot be easily applied to permanent-capacitor single-phase machines; ii) stray flux analysis reveals the presence of additional harmonic sidebands, even in healthy three-phase induction motors; iii) a rough analysis of the third harmonic in the current spectrum may be sufficient to diagnose the single phasing fault.

articleTitle: Static, Dynamic and Mixed Eccentricity Fault Detection Using MCSA and Stray Flux Monitoring via Finite Element Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: This paper analyzes detection methods of static eccentricity (SE), dynamic eccentricity (DE) and mixed eccentricity (ME) faults in a squirrel-cage induction motor (IM) by finite element analysis (FEA). Many methods have been created to identify and differentiate these faults, enabling appropriate safety precautions to be implemented to reduce their impact. Motor current signature analysis (MCSA) as well as the stray flux of the motor is used in order to verify whether these techniques can identify the presence of the three different types of eccentricity faults. Also, since the researched motor produces Principal Slot Harmonics (PSH), the zero-sequence current spectrum is investigated (SFD-MCSA Method) in the case of only-static eccentricity. The work is carried out with transient simulations using the commercially available finite element package - Ansys Maxwell.

articleTitle: Fault-Tolerant Analysis of Kalman Filter Sensor Fusion for Sensorless Control of a Multiphase Machine
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE 14th International Symposium on Diagnostics for Electrical Machines, Power Electronics and Drives (SDEMPED)
abstract: This paper investigates the feasibility and the performance of a Kalman filter sensor fusion in a sensorless drive. The algorithm is developed for a six-phase synchronous reluctance motor. Multi-stator (MS) approach is used to decompose the machine into two three-phase windings. Each winding is supplied by a dedicated inverter and a position estimation algorithm is implemented for each system resulting into two estimated positions. Firstly, the performance of the Kalman fusion algorithm are compared with a non-weighted average by analyzing different supply scenarios. Then, a sensorless control strategy for a multiphase machine is proposed in the case of a fault in the position sensor. Both control loops are closed on the estimated position from the Kalman fusion algorithm and the motor is able to operate sensorless with good performance without using complex compensation methods. The developed sensorless control strategy is validated through an extensive experimental stage.
